key_insight: Training GPT-style models on synthetic limit order book streams reveals that they learn amortized Bayesian inference over market regimes, not just next-token statistics.
engineering_relevance: The study shows foundation-model pretraining can recover latent simulator parameters and transfer to real NASDAQ order flow, suggesting a path to more interpretable and data-efficient market microstructure models.
method: Train autoregressive transformers on synthetic order-flow sequences from simulators with known latent states.
Benchmark predictions against exact Bayes-optimal and oracle predictors using entropy-aware evaluation.
Probe frozen activations with linear readouts to decode latent regimes and test zero-shot transfer to real data.
evidence_signal: The model’s next-token predictions match the exact Bayes optimum to within a millinat per token, latent regimes are linearly decodable, and enriched simulator mixtures improve zero-shot NASDAQ transfer.
watch_item: Results depend strongly on how well the simulator prior covers real market flow, so mismatch between synthetic and real regimes may limit deployment.
paper_title: What Do Foundation Models for Market Microstructure Learn? A Controlled Study with Synthetic Limit Order Books
